answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis makes each agent earn trust slowly: newcomers start with tiny limits, and every verified task adds a rung they cannot buy in bulk. Cheap fake identities starve because honest work is the only nectar that feeds reputation, and a river of Sybil accounts trying to flood the market would each need months of real, costly service before moving meaningful value, so forging a thousand credible agents costs far more than the fraud could ever return.
